The Feasts of the Most High

precepts.text: Moses gave the instruction to separate cities of refuge in the midst of the land; in Joshua 20 Joshua is applying the law.
precepts.point: Notice the scripture says slayer, not murderer: a slayer may be innocent, it may have been a mistake or self-defense, so there are stipulations and laws for his case.
precepts.why:
Now that every tribe had its inheritance, the cities of refuge had to be instituted, “whereof I spake unto you by the hand of Moses”. Here is where Moses spoke it: “When the Lord thy God hath cut off the nations, whose land the Lord thy God giveth thee, and thou succeedest them, and dwellest in their cities, and in their houses; Thou shalt separate three cities for thee in the midst of thy land”. The coasts of the land were to be divided into three parts, “that every slayer may flee thither.”

Moses gave the instruction; in Joshua 20 Joshua is applying the law, now that the nations are cut off and Israel dwells in their cities.

precepts.text: The case of the slayer: two neighbours go into the wood to hew wood, the axe head slips from the helve and lights upon his neighbour that he die; he hated him not in time past, so he was not worthy of death.
precepts.point: Notice the scripture says slayer, not murderer: a slayer may be innocent, it may have been a mistake or self-defense, so there are stipulations and laws for his case.
precepts.why:
“That the slayer that killeth any person unawares and unwittingly may flee thither”. Unwittingly means unknowingly; remember the word wittingly in Genesis 48, where Israel guided his hands knowing what he was doing. This is accidental death, not intentional murder. “And this is the case of the slayer, which shall flee thither, that he may live: Whoso killeth his neighbour ignorantly, whom he hated not in time past”. Two neighbours go into the wood to hew wood, “and the head slippeth from the helve, and lighteth upon his neighbour, that he die; he shall flee unto one of those cities, and live”. It is like leaving a co-worker shut in the freezer by mistake because you were focused on going home.

Notice the scripture says slayer, not murderer: a slayer may be innocent, it may have been a mistake or self-defense, so there are stipulations and laws for his case. He “was not worthy of death, inasmuch as he hated him not in time past.”

“Lest the avenger of the blood pursue the slayer, while his heart is hot, and overtake him, because the way is long, and slay him”. The avenger of blood is a family member of the one killed, and while his heart is hot he is not thinking logically; he is guided by his emotions, and that is how you end up rendering evil for evil. Heart is hot is the same way we talk today, I was hot, I am heated: our forefathers and foremothers spoke the same way.

precepts.text: The cities of refuge were appointed that the manslayer die not, until he stand before the congregation in judgment.
precepts.point: Notice the scripture says slayer, not murderer: a slayer may be innocent, it may have been a mistake or self-defense, so there are stipulations and laws for his case.
precepts.why:
“Then ye shall appoint you cities to be cities of refuge for you; that the slayer may flee thither, which killeth any person at unawares. And they shall be unto you cities for refuge from the avenger; that the manslayer die not, until he stand before the congregation in judgment.”

This is the same law Joshua is applying: refuge from the avenger of blood for the one who killed at unawares. The city did not settle the matter; it kept the manslayer alive until he could stand before the congregation in judgment and his case be heard.

precepts.text: The law goes back to Exodus: he that smiteth a man that he die shall surely be put to death, but if a man lie not in wait and God deliver him into his hand, a place is appointed whither he shall flee.
precepts.point: Notice the scripture says slayer, not murderer: a slayer may be innocent, it may have been a mistake or self-defense, so there are stipulations and laws for his case.
precepts.why:
The law goes back to Exodus. “He that smiteth a man, so that he die, shall be surely put to death.” But: “And if a man lie not in wait, but God deliver him into his hand; then I will appoint thee a place whither he shall flee.” The place appointed whither he shall flee is the city of refuge Joshua is now setting up.

The line is drawn right there: the one who lies in wait is put to death; the one who did not lie in wait, whom God delivered into his hand, has a place to flee. That is the difference between the murderer and the slayer who killed unawares and unwittingly.

precepts.text: Nehemiah said, if ye do so again, I will lay hands on you; the same spirit and speech is in our people to this day.
precepts.point: The avenger of blood is a family member of the one killed, and while his heart is hot he is not thinking logically; he is guided by his emotions, and that is how you end up rendering evil for evil. Heart is hot is the same way we talk today, I was hot, I am heated: our forefathers and foremothers spoke the same way.
precepts.why:
“Then I testified against them, and said unto them, Why lodge ye about the wall? if ye do so again, I will lay hands on you.” I will lay hands on you: that is how Nehemiah talked, and that is how we talk. The same spirit and speech is in our people to this day.

It is the same with the avenger of blood whose heart is hot: heart is hot is the same way we talk today, I was hot, I am heated. Our forefathers and foremothers spoke the same way we do.

precepts.text: But if any man hate his neighbour and lie in wait and smite him mortally, the elders of his city shall fetch him from the refuge and deliver him to the avenger of blood; thine eye shall not pity him.
precepts.point: The avenger of blood is a family member of the one killed, and while his heart is hot he is not thinking logically; he is guided by his emotions, and that is how you end up rendering evil for evil. Heart is hot is the same way we talk today, I was hot, I am heated: our forefathers and foremothers spoke the same way.
precepts.why:
The murderer cannot run to a city of refuge to lay low; those cities were not established for him. “But if any man hate his neighbour, and lie in wait for him, and rise up against him, and smite him mortally that he die, and fleeth into one of these cities: Then the elders of his city shall send and fetch him thence, and deliver him into the hand of the avenger of blood, that he may die. Thine eye shall not pity him”.

Even today a killer can cross the border into another jurisdiction and go free, and that is evil; but when Israel controlled the land you could not cross a border to get away with murder, for the elders would deliver you right back to the city you came from. Your sin will find you out. That is how “thou shalt put away the guilt of innocent blood from Israel, that it may go well with thee.”

precepts.text: Life shall go for life, eye for eye, tooth for tooth: that was the judgment instituted in that time; today we are under different laws of the land, and you forgive your brother seventy times seven.
precepts.point: The avenger of blood is a family member of the one killed, and while his heart is hot he is not thinking logically; he is guided by his emotions, and that is how you end up rendering evil for evil. Heart is hot is the same way we talk today, I was hot, I am heated: our forefathers and foremothers spoke the same way.
precepts.why:
“And thine eye shall not pity; but life shall go for life, eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot.” That was the judgment instituted in that time: the murderer delivered to the avenger of blood, life for life, without pity.

Today we are under different laws of the land, and you forgive your brother seventy times seven. But the cities of refuge in Joshua were built under that judgment, which is why the murderer had no refuge in them and the slayer who killed unawares did.

precepts.text: If he thrust him suddenly without enmity, or cast a stone seeing him not, the congregation shall judge between the slayer and the revenger of blood and deliver the innocent slayer back to his city of refuge.
precepts.point: The avenger of blood is a family member of the one killed, and while his heart is hot he is not thinking logically; he is guided by his emotions, and that is how you end up rendering evil for evil. Heart is hot is the same way we talk today, I was hot, I am heated: our forefathers and foremothers spoke the same way.
precepts.why:
“But if he thrust him suddenly without enmity, or have cast upon him any thing without laying of wait, Or with any stone, wherewith a man may die, seeing him not, and cast it upon him, that he die, and was not his enemy, neither sought his harm: Then the congregation shall judge between the slayer and the revenger of blood according to these judgments”.

The innocent slayer, the one who killed without enmity and seeing him not, gets his case judged. “And the congregation shall deliver the slayer out of the hand of the revenger of blood, and the congregation shall restore him to the city of his refuge, whither he was fled: and he shall abide in it unto the death of the high priest, which was anointed with the holy oil.” So the refuge from the avenger of blood in Joshua 20 works like this: the congregation judges, the innocent slayer is delivered from the revenger and sent back to his city of refuge, and he stays there until the high priest dies.

precepts.text: The congregation shall restore him to the city of his refuge, and he shall abide in it unto the death of the high priest, which was anointed with the holy oil.
precepts.point: He also dwelt there until the death of the high priest of those days; then the slayer shall return to his own city and his own house, the city from whence he fled.
precepts.why:
“And he shall dwell in that city, until he stand before the congregation for judgment”. The congregation had to see whether it was a mistake or intentional, questioning him on what he was doing and why, just like a courtroom. When the judgment came back that it was not intentional: “And the congregation shall deliver the slayer out of the hand of the revenger of blood, and the congregation shall restore him to the city of his refuge, whither he was fled: and he shall abide in it unto the death of the high priest, which was anointed with the holy oil.”

That is the “until the death of the high priest that shall be in those days” of Joshua 20:6. The slayer was restored to his city of refuge and abode there until the anointed high priest died; then he returned to his own city and his own house.

precepts.text: If the slayer comes outside the border of his city of refuge before the death of the high priest and the revenger of blood finds him and kills him, the revenger shall not be guilty of blood; the refuge is protective custody, and he was to remain in it.
precepts.point: He also dwelt there until the death of the high priest of those days; then the slayer shall return to his own city and his own house, the city from whence he fled.
precepts.why:
The refuge was protective custody, and the slayer was to remain in it. “But if the slayer shall at any time come without the border of the city of his refuge, whither he was fled; And the revenger of blood find him without the borders of the city of his refuge, and the revenger of blood kill the slayer; he shall not be guilty of blood: Because he should have remained in the city of his refuge until the death of the high priest”.

If he stepped outside the border before the high priest died and the revenger of blood found him and killed him, the revenger was not guilty. “but after the death of the high priest the slayer shall return into the land of his possession.” That is the return in Joshua 20:6: “then shall the slayer return, and come unto his own city, and unto his own house, unto the city from whence he fled.”

precepts.text: At the mouth of two witnesses or three witnesses shall he that is worthy of death be put to death; at the mouth of one witness he shall not be put to death.
precepts.point: These cities were appointed for all the children of Israel and for the stranger that sojourneth among them, that whosoever killeth any person at unawares might flee thither and not die by the hand of the avenger of blood, until he stood before the congregation: until he gets a fair trial.
precepts.why:
The cities were appointed so that the one who killed at unawares would “not die by the hand of the avenger of blood, until he stood before the congregation”: until he gets a fair trial. That trial had a standard. “At the mouth of two witnesses, or three witnesses, shall he that is worthy of death be put to death; but at the mouth of one witness he shall not be put to death.”

No man was put to death on one man's word. This law of righteous judgment is what is missing in the cursed cities of our people, the so-called Blacks, Hispanics, and Native Americans, who have not learned to apply the scripture and await righteous trial.

precepts.text: If thy brother trespass against thee, go and tell him his fault alone; if he will not hear, take one or two more, that in the mouth of two or three witnesses every word may be established, and then tell it unto the church.
precepts.point: These cities were appointed for all the children of Israel and for the stranger that sojourneth among them, that whosoever killeth any person at unawares might flee thither and not die by the hand of the avenger of blood, until he stood before the congregation: until he gets a fair trial.
precepts.why:
“Moreover if thy brother shall trespass against thee, go and tell him his fault between thee and him alone: if he shall hear thee, thou hast gained thy brother.” If your brother trespasses against you, you do not go and shoot, stab, or fight him; you speak to him alone. “But if he will not hear thee, then take with thee one or two more, that in the mouth of two or three witnesses every word may be established”, the same two or three witnesses of Deuteronomy 17; and if he neglects to hear them, “tell it unto the church”.

But not everything is a Matthew 18. Matthew 18 goes into severe sin, a matter worthy of putting somebody out of the body, “as an heathen man and a publican”, not a petty disagreement over a parking space, a stepped-on toe, or a mispronounced name. That is the righteous judgment the cities of refuge stood for: a man does not die by a hot heart, he stands before the congregation.

precepts.text: Admonish a friend, for many times it is a slander; believe not every tale, and do not threaten a Matthew 18 over what only needs a correction.
precepts.point: Not everything is a Matthew 18: Matthew 18 goes into severe sin, a matter worthy of putting somebody out of the body, not a petty disagreement over a parking space, a stepped-on toe, or a mispronounced name. For the petty offenses the scripture says admonish a friend, because many times what you heard is just a tale.
precepts.why:
For the petty offenses the scripture says admonish a friend. “Admonish a friend, it may be he hath not done it: and if he have done it, that he do it no more. Admonish thy friend, it may be he hath not said it: and if he have, that he speak it not again. Admonish a friend: for many times it is a slander, and believe not every tale.” Many times what you heard is just a tale. “There is one that slippeth in his speech, but not from his heart; and who is he that hath not offended with his tongue?”

“Admonish thy neighbour before thou threaten him; and not being angry, give place to the law of the most High.” Do not threaten a Matthew 18 over what only needs a correction. And when you are angry you are not thinking logically; precepts are not coming to your mind, only carnal solutions. Do not go and talk to a brother while you are upset, and do not cleave to another backbiter or gossiper to feed your anger; cleave to somebody positive that is a peacemaker and solution minded.

Give place to the law of the Most High: whatever situation you are going through, the solution is in the Bible, so do not let anger close the book on you.

precepts.text: Offences will come, it is inevitable; we build stronger bonds with brothers and sisters through adversity, so endeavor to keep the unity.
precepts.point: Not everything is a Matthew 18: Matthew 18 goes into severe sin, a matter worthy of putting somebody out of the body, not a petty disagreement over a parking space, a stepped-on toe, or a mispronounced name. For the petty offenses the scripture says admonish a friend, because many times what you heard is just a tale.
precepts.why:
“Then said he unto the disciples, It is impossible but that offences will come: but woe unto him, through whom they come!” Offences will come; it is inevitable. Even in Israel there were slayers and avengers of blood, which is why the cities of refuge existed at all.

So when the offence comes, do not be the one through whom it comes. We build stronger bonds with brothers and sisters through adversity, so endeavor to keep the unity.

precepts.text: The spirit of anger and hatred transitions to murder; whosoever hateth his brother is a murderer.
precepts.point: Not everything is a Matthew 18: Matthew 18 goes into severe sin, a matter worthy of putting somebody out of the body, not a petty disagreement over a parking space, a stepped-on toe, or a mispronounced name. For the petty offenses the scripture says admonish a friend, because many times what you heard is just a tale.
precepts.why:
“Whosoever hateth his brother is a murderer: and ye know that no murderer hath eternal life abiding in him.” The spirit of anger and hatred transitions to murder. That is the avenger of blood with his heart hot, and that is why the man who killed at unawares had a city to flee to until he stood before the congregation.

When you are angry you are not thinking logically; only carnal solutions come to mind. Hatred of your brother is already murder in the eyes of the Most High, so deal with the anger before it goes where it is going.

precepts.text: This is thankworthy, if a man for conscience toward God endure grief, suffering wrongfully; but examine yourself before you use this precept to play the victim, for the Lord knows what is behind closed doors.
precepts.point: Give place to the law of the Most High: whatever situation you are going through, the solution is in the Bible, so do not let anger close the book on you. Sometimes the answer is to suffer wrongfully, and what matters is not who is right but what the right thing to do is according to the Bible.
precepts.why:
“For this is thankworthy, if a man for conscience toward God endure grief, suffering wrongfully.” Sometimes the answer is to suffer wrongfully. What matters is not who is right but what the right thing to do is according to the Bible.

But examine yourself before you use this precept to play the victim, for the Lord knows what is behind closed doors. Give place to the law of the Most High; the solution to whatever you are going through is in the Bible.

They appointed Kedesh in Galilee in mount Naphtali, Shechem in mount Ephraim, and Kirjath-arba, which is Hebron, in the mountain of Judah; and on the other side Jordan by Jericho they assigned Bezer out of the tribe of Reuben, Ramoth in Gilead out of the tribe of Gad, and Golan in Bashan out of the tribe of Manasseh.

These cities were appointed for all the children of Israel and for the stranger that sojourneth among them, that whosoever killeth any person at unawares might flee thither and not die by the hand of the avenger of blood, until he stood before the congregation: until he gets a fair trial.
